question: Why were some of the Parthenon sculptures in London scraped with copper tools in 1937?
answer: To make them whiter. Joseph Duveen, the dealer paying for their new gallery, wanted white marble, and workmen used copper tools and carborundum, a hard abrasive, to strip a brownish surface layer that may have held ancient finish. An internal inquiry in 1938 called the damage obvious. The full story came out only in the late 1990s.
move: A patron paying for the display can end up deciding what the object is.
reference: Ian Jenkins, Cleaning and Controversy: The Parthenon Sculptures 1811–1939, British Museum Occasional Paper 146, 2001
